rope.working_end: the person's RIGHT end (table -y; image right in the top-down shots); its tip is the darker end, in view from 20.0 s
rope.fraction_basis: rope_fraction = s_from_tip_m / 1.05 (REAL2SIM's assumed length; the far end is never seen) -- use s_from_tip_m
rope.frames: path / centreline / xy: table metres in the shot's frame, origin at the image centre, x away from the person, y to the person's left

events.note: pinches the standing part well left of where the loop will be (its arc from the tip read at 20.0 s, when the tip is in view)
takes the rope near its right end (the end is off-frame right until 19.9 s); at 20.0 s the hand holds the fold: the end's run enters it at the first value, the standing part leaves it at the second
folds the end back to the left in the air and lays it on the FAR side (+x) of the standing part, pointing left (20.0 s); no crossing yet
lets the standing part go and moves to the middle
takes the end's run ~0.15-0.18 m from the tip, between the tip and the right hand's fold

draws the end left and lays it ACROSS the standing part from the far side to the near side: crossing X1, the end OVER the standing part, made under the left hand's fingers (seen at 21.0-21.3 s: the end hangs toward the person from X1)
pinches X1 (thumb on top) from here to the end of step 2; it slides the rope through X1 while the loop is sized (21.3-25.0 s)
still holding the fold (the loop's far end), swings it away from the person (+x): the oval loop turns into a loop pointing away
lets the loop go; it lies on the table, pointing away from the person
takes the end close to its tip and draws it out while the left hand holds X1: the loop shrinks (0.66 m of rope at 21.3 s -> 0.48 m at 22.7 s -> 0.39 m at 25.0 s)

the left hand keeps X1 pinched between thumb and fingers; the strands at X1, and the loop strand just past it on the standing-part side (where the end will pass under), are held off the table by the fingers. Stationary through the tuck (fingertip moves < 1 cm 26.0-29.7 s). The strand it holds up is the one the end goes under: s_from_tip is that strand's pass at X2, read at 32.0 s
takes the end ~0.13 m from its tip (the hand is mostly off the right of the frame; the value is the tip-to-frame-edge arc at 29.3 s, a lower bound)
lifts the end from the lower right and lays it up and across the loop's right side into the eye (OVER that side); the path is the tip's
brings the tip down across the eye to just beside the left hand's X1
the index finger tucks the tip UNDER the loop strand next to X1, the one the left hand holds up (crossing X2: the end under). Mostly occluded by the fingers; the result is read at 32.0 s
draws the tip up through the eye and out to the right, OVER the loop's far (right) side (crossing X3: the end over); the knot is formed, loose
the right hand leaves the frame
lets X1 go; the loose knot lies on its own (31.7-33.4 s)
takes the standing part just left of the knot (its arc from the tip composed from the 33.6 s tail and the 32.0 s knot)
takes the end right of the knot, ~5-9 cm from the tip
draws the standing part away to the left (+y) along the rope; it leaves the frame at ~35.3 s, so the distance (to 35.3 s) is a lower bound
draws the end away to the right (-y) along the rope (distance to 35.7 s); the knot closes to ~4-5 cm

key_shapes.label: straight
key_shapes.note: both ends off-frame; the left hand pinches the rope at the left

key_shapes.label: fold
key_shapes.note: the right hand has taken the rope near its right end and folded the end back leftward, on the far side (+x) of the standing part

key_shapes.label: take_end
key_shapes.note: the left hand has let the standing part go and pinches the end's run in the middle; the right hand still holds the fold

key_shapes.label: loop_oval
key_shapes.note: the oval between the hands; X1 and the tip are under the left hand, the fold under the right

key_shapes.label: turn_loop
key_shapes.note: X1 made (under the left hand), the end hangs toward the person; the right hand lifts the fold away (+x) to turn the loop
key_shapes.centred_on: X1 (the end-over-standing crossing; for the loose knot the last one met from the end)

key_shapes.label: loop
key_shapes.note: teardrop loop pointing away (+x); X1 at its bottom by the left hand; the right hand holds the end
key_shapes.centred_on: X1 (the end-over-standing crossing; for the loose knot the last one met from the end)

key_shapes.label: loop_closeup
key_shapes.note: rotated close-up of the same loop: the crossing at 15.6 px per rope width
key_shapes.centred_on: X1 (the end-over-standing crossing; for the loose knot the last one met from the end)

key_shapes.label: tuck_over
key_shapes.note: step 2: the right hand has brought the end up from the lower right and across the loop's right side into the eye (over it); only the run from the tip to the right hand is traced

key_shapes.label: loose
key_shapes.start: right edge (the working end; tip off-frame right)
key_shapes.note: the loose knot, no hands; motion-blurred zoom
key_shapes.centred_on: X1 (the end-over-standing crossing; for the loose knot the last one met from the end)

key_shapes.label: pull_start
key_shapes.note: step 3 begins: the right hand holds the end right of the knot, the left the standing part left of it; the knot body's order is read from 32.0 (too small here to trace)

key_shapes.label: pulling
key_shapes.note: both hands drawing the tails apart; tail traced from the tip to the knot

key_shapes.label: tight
key_shapes.start: right hand (tip at the right edge)
key_shapes.note: the knot ~4 cm across; the left hand has left the frame

after_step1.words: one crossing X1: the end OVER the standing part; walking from the standing part: X1 under, up the loop's right side, across its far end right-to-left, down its left side, X1 over, then the end toward the person and right

after_step2.words: X3 (met first from the tip): the end OVER the loop's far side; X2: the end UNDER the loop strand just past X1 on the standing side; X1: the end OVER the standing part. An alternating 3-crossing diagram: the overhand knot (trefoil)

after_step3.words: the same three crossings drawn tight (~4 cm): too small in the wide shot to read over/under (assumed unchanged: pulling the tails does not change the code)

retarget_numbers.basis: arc length from the working end's tip [m], table metres; the working end is the person's RIGHT end

d_grab_step1.how: 20.0 s: the right hand's fold; first value = where the end's run enters the hand (measured), second = where the standing part leaves it; the apex lies between

d_take_end_step1.how: 20.4 s: the left hand's pinch on the end's run, the point it carries over the standing part

loop_circumference.note: the right hand draws the end out while the left holds X1, so the loop shrinks; 20.9 s excludes the rope under the left hand

loop_size_wxh.note: extent [x, y] of the loop between X1's two passes, table metres

d_grab_step2.how: 29.3 s: tip to where the end leaves the frame under the right hand (lower bound)

loose_knot_32.0.how: arcs within the knot measured at 32.0 s (from where the end leaves the frame); the tail from the tip to X3 measured at 33.6 s (wide shot) and added

tail_lengths.standing_tail: not measurable: the far end is never in view (REAL2SIM assumed 1.05 m in all)

step3.note: pull = fingertip displacement from 33.6 s to 35.3 s (left: it then leaves the frame, a lower bound) / 35.7 s (right). Ring extents [along x (away), along y (sideways)] from the rope mask above the tails' line. The 32.0 s ring (close-up scale) and the 33.6 s ring (wide scale) differ by ~50%: the hands re-handled the knot across the cut, and each shot's scale is only good to ~10-15%

manual: key-frame route waypoints (KEYS in demo_extract.py) were read off gridded stills by eye; the traced centrelines, arc lengths, crossings and over/under come from the image (mask, distance transform, intensity profiles)
